arguments.court_reasoning: Court found video recording not played or disclosed; no opportunity to observe witness under questioning; recording insufficient to remedy absence and anonymity.

arguments.claim: Trial court did not explain or assess grave danger justifying concealment of witness X’s identity or examination in absence of parties; no balancing exercise between defence rights and witness protection.

anchor.surface_text: However, the trial court did not explain at all the grave danger examining witness X before it and in the presence of the parties would entail. Neither did the Trabzon Assize Court indicate any specific reasons regarding the need to examine him in the absence of the parties. Furthermore, the Court finds it significant that neither the trial court nor the Trabzon Assize Court made any assessment of the question as to whether less stringent alternatives would be sufficient, which would indicate that they had indeed carried out a balancing exercise, albeit implicitly, between the rights of the defence and those of the victims and the witnesses.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court emphasized need for individualized assessment and balancing of rights; absence of such reasoning undermined fairness.

arguments.claim: Trial court did not approach evidence of witness X with caution or assess reliability given absence from trial; no examination of reliability of statements.

anchor.surface_text: Similarly, there is also no indication in the case file showing that the national courts either approached the evidence given by witness X with any particular caution or that they were aware that it carried less weight owing to his absence from the trial. More importantly, none of the national courts embarked upon an examination of the reliability of the statements of witness X either.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court found failure to assess reliability or weight of evidence undermined fairness of trial.

arguments.claim: Applicant did not waive rights under Article 6 § 3 (d) to test truthfulness of eyewitness; failure to put questions or object does not imply waiver given importance of witness.

anchor.surface_text: Therefore, the Court is not convinced that the applicant waived his rights under Article 6 § 3 (d) of the Convention to test the truthfulness of the only direct eyewitness in the present case.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court distinguished from cases where waiver was found; here applicant consistently objected and requested examination.

arguments.claim: Possibility to put written questions to absent witness is not a panacea and cannot substitute fundamental right to examine witness in person, especially when no good reason for absence exists.

anchor.surface_text: The Court further notes that the possibility to put written questions to an absent witness should not be regarded as a panacea remedying the absence of an important witness from the trial and the resulting prejudice the trial court’s use of his or her evidence entailed to the rights of the defence irrespective of the individual circumstances of a given case.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court emphasized that written questions do not compensate for unjustified absence of witness.

arguments.claim: Trial court did not respond to applications to have witness X give evidence in person or to put questions to him; no indication applications would have had different outcome.

anchor.surface_text: Yet, the trial court did not provide an answer to that application. Moreover, whilst the applicant and his lawyer consistently raised their objections to the examination of witness X by another court and they repeatedly invited the trial court to secure his appearance in person so that they could cross‑examine and question him, the trial court did not even respond to some of those applications.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court found trial court’s indifference to applications undermined fairness and remedial possibilities.

arguments.claim: Video recording of witness X’s statements was not disclosed to applicant; playing it would have rendered protection measure futile; recording not mentioned or assessed in trial court judgment.

anchor.surface_text: The Court notes that although the Government argued that the applicant could have asked to have a copy of the videotaped statements of witness X, they failed to explain on what legal basis he would have been able to do so, given that the trial court had opted to protect him by withholding his true identity throughout the proceedings in accordance with Article 58 § 2 and 3 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Indeed, had the applicant been allowed to obtain a copy of the videotaped statement, it would have effectively rendered that protection measure futile.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court found video recording insufficient safeguard given secrecy and lack of disclosure.

arguments.claim: Existence of video recording alone does not cure inability to observe credibility and reliability of witness under questioning; witness evidence remained untested.

anchor.surface_text: Even assuming that the trial court had indeed considered and examined the videotaped statements of witness X, which could have given its judges the opportunity to observe his demeanour, that fact alone would not have altered the fact that both the trial court and the applicant and his lawyer had not had the possibility to observe the credibility and the reliability of witness X under questioning as he was not subjected to questioning by the Trabzon Assize Court, which merely took his statements and asked him to make an identification on the basis of the applicant’s photograph.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court emphasized importance of direct examination and cross-examination for testing reliability.

arguments.claim: Applicant was not afforded proper safeguards commensurate with nature of complaints and seriousness of life imprisonment to sufficiently test reliability and truthfulness of witness X’s evidence.

anchor.surface_text: Accordingly, the foregoing considerations allow the Court to conclude that the applicant was not afforded proper safeguards commensurate with the nature of his complaints and the importance of what was at stake for him, namely life imprisonment, enabling him to sufficiently test the reliability and truthfulness of evidence given by witness X in line with the guarantees of a fair trial under Article 6 of the Convention.

arguments.court_reasoning: Court found violation of Article 6 §§ 1 and 3 (d) due to lack of safeguards and inability to test evidence reliability.
